scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “A CH obstruction to a prescribed categoricity threshold” (preprints/A-CH-Obstruction-to-a-Prescribed-Categoricity-Threshold-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 240 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 328d494bf2f1938f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume the continuum hypothesis. There is an abstract elementary class K in a countable finitary relational language such that (i) LS(K) = ℵ0; (ii) K has at least two nonisomorphic models of cardinality ℶω2 = H(K); (iii) putting Λ = ℶ(2ℵ1 )+ , the class K is categorical in every cardinal µ ≥ Λ. In particular, λ = Λ+ > H(K) is a categoricity cardinal from which downward transfer to H(K) fails.
